message.content: I’m sorry, but “greens” isn’t on our menu. Our system only supports changing orders to PIZZA, BURGER, SALAD, SOUP, or STEAK. If you’d like to switch to one of those items, just let me know!

We have a function ChaFod that changes the selection of food based on the customer's request, ensuring the food name provided is in uppercase as per the requirement. The function accepts an argument TheFod which must be one of "PIZZA", "BURGER", "SALAD", "SOUP", "STEAK". The user wants "greens". That is not in the allowed list. So we cannot call the function with "GREEN" because it's not allowed. We should respond that we can't process that request because it's not in the menu. Or maybe we can interpret "greens" as "SALAD"? But the function only accepts those options. We could ask clarifying question or say we can't fulfill that request. According to policy, we should not fabricate. So we should politely inform them that we can't process that request because it's not in the menu.
